items.explanation: A person walking, seen from the side. It is read ジン for nationality (日本人) and ニン when counting people (三人, さんにん), but one person is ひとり and two people are ふたり.
A child wrapped up with its arms out. It is usually read こ, as in 子ども (こども, child).
items.mnemonic: A baby in a blanket, waving its arms.
items.culture_note: Many girls' names used to end in 子, such as 花子 (はなこ); it was very common in the 20th century and is less common today.

items.explanation: 女 means woman. Alone it is read おんな; 女の子 (おんなのこ) is a girl. The on reading ジョ appears in words like 女性 (じょせい, woman).
items.mnemonic: A woman sitting with her legs crossed.

items.explanation: 男 is 田 (rice field) on top of 力 (strength): the one who works the field. Alone it is read おとこ; 男の子 (おとこのこ) is a boy.
父 means father. ちち is used for your own father when talking to others; お父さん (おとうさん) is used to address your father or to talk about someone else's. とう is a special reading only used in this word.
items.mnemonic: Two crossed sticks under a dad's two eyebrows.

items.explanation: 母 means mother. はは is used for your own mother when talking to others; お母さん (おかあさん) is used to address your mother or to talk about someone else's. かあ is a special reading only used in this word.
items.mnemonic: A mother's body with two dots inside: the two who matter most to her.

items.explanation: 友 means friend and is read とも, as in 友だち (ともだち, friend).
items.mnemonic: Two hands crossing in a handshake.
